name: Sit to stand
summary: Stand up from a chair and sit back down without using the hands.
setup: A firm chair, side-on to the phone. Feet flat and slightly back, lean forward from the hips, stand fully tall, then lower slowly until you touch the seat.
brief: A firm chair. Feet flat and slightly back, lean forward from the hips, stand fully tall, then lower slowly until you touch the seat.
why: Side-on the knee angle runs from about 90° to straight every rep, so each stand is counted. Whether the hands helped is not reliably visible, so form is listed rather than judged.
progression: Lower chair; arms crossed; hold a weight.
regression: Higher seat, or a light push from the hands.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Pushing up with the hands
faults.tip: Cross the arms over the chest so the legs must do all the work.

faults.label: Dropping into the seat
faults.tip: The sit-down is half the exercise. Take three seconds and touch the seat lightly.

faults.label: Dropping into the chair
faults.tip: Falling into the seat skips the hardest and most useful part of the movement.

faults.label: Throwing the body forward
faults.tip: A controlled forward lean is right; a lunge of the head and shoulders is momentum.

guide.surface: A stable chair against a wall so it cannot slide.
guide.stop: Dizziness, or knee pain on the way down.
guide.cannotSee: The hands pushing on the thighs or the chair.

points.t: Flat, slightly behind the knees, hip-width apart.
Nose over toes to start the stand, then tall at the top.
